finding: The reverse reference gait at -0.074 is open-loop stable, so a viable reverse gait DOES exist in the dataset. The learned policies from v12 to v17 all fall after ~2 s, so the remaining problem is policy tracking of that reference, not the absence of a reverse gait.
test: diagnostics/test_ref_stability.py - replay each reference joint trajectory open-loop as position targets from the home keyframe, 5 s, flat terrain.
note: The negative final heights (-0.15 m) of the two failing replays are the no-body-collision artefact: once tipped past recovery the robot has no torso contact geometry and sinks through the floor. This is why falls are terminal in scene_flat_terrain (see make_getup_model.py).

v17_result.config: curriculum -0.06..-0.09 (grid-aligned to -0.074), imitation 0.5 and 1.0, restored from v15
v17_result.conclusion: Speed improves to -0.11 m/s (the fastest reverse gait measured), but stability does not: both still fall in 1.6-2.6 s. The imitation weight (1.0, i.e. 15 after the internal joint-pos factor) is small next to normalized_progress (80), so the stable reference does not dominate.

next: Weight the now-proven-stable -0.074 reference heavily (imitation 8 and 20) so it dominates the progress term; runs launched as backward_v18_imit8p0 / backward_v18_imit20p0.
